title: Dragon Door
body:
Goal: practice and, or and f-strings.

The dragon door opens if:

  • you have the golden key and you are level 3 or more, or
  • you are level 10 or more (legends do not need keys).
  1. Open starter.py in Thonny.
  2. TODO 1: change the if line in door_opens(). Brackets help: (has_key and level >= 3) or level >= 10.
  3. TODO 2: make the welcome message use an f-string with the hero name.
  4. Run it with these answers and check the door does the right thing: key yes + level 5 (opens), key yes + level 2 (shut), key no + level 12 (opens).

Extra: add a third way in: a secret password typed by the player. (Only a made-up game password, never a real one!)

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Read the three rules for the door at the top of the starter file. Right now door_opens() only checks the key. Does it ever look at the level?

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Join two true-or-false checks with and when both must be true. Join them with or when either one is enough. Brackets ( ) keep a pair of checks together. For the message, an f-string puts a variable inside curly braces.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: The if line has this shape: if (____ and ____) or ____:. Match each blank to one of the rules. For the welcome, start the text with f and put the hero name inside braces, like print(f"... {____} ...").

starter.name: starter.py
starter.html: # Dragon Door # The dragon door opens if you have the golden key AND you are level 3 or # more, OR if you are level 10 or more (legends do not need keys). def door_opens(has_key, level): """Return True if the dragon door opens, otherwise False.""" # TODO 1: change this line. Use "and", "or" and brackets ( ). if has_key: return True else: return False if __name__ == "__main__": hero = input("Hero name (make one up): ") key_answer = input("Do you have the golden key? (yes/no) ") has_key = key_answer.lower() == "yes" level = int(input("What level are you? ")) if door_opens(has_key, level): # TODO 2: use an f-string so the message says the hero's name. print("The dragon door creaks open. Welcome!") else: print("The door stays shut. Find the key or reach level 10.")
